nodes_add.name: Nitya Tripta (S. Balakrishna Pillai)
nodes_add.note: Student of Atmananda who kept notes of his talks 1950-1959, published 1963.

nodes_add.name: K. Padmanabha Menon (Sri Adwayananda)
nodes_add.note: Atmananda's eldest son; taught at Anandawadi until 2001; compiled Atmananda Tattwa Samhita (1973) from tape recordings.

nodes_add.name: Hari Gopalan Citar
nodes_add.note: Disciple to whom followers say the Akilathirattu Ammanai was dictated; spelled Arigopalan Citar in some Wikipedia passages.

edges_upsert.note: Eldest son; continued the teaching at Anandawadi until 2001 (Wikipedia).
Followers say the Akilam was dictated to him; Wikipedia gives 1841 (Ayyavazhi; 10 December 1841 on the Vaikundar page) and 11 December 1840 (timeline).

places.name: Yangon (Rangoon)
places.what: Lived with her husband from about 1925; first retreat at the Kamayut Meditation Center; practice at Mahasi's centre

places.name: Rasta Peth, Pune
places.what: Ganesh temple where the first jnana yajna opened on 31 December 1951 (approximate)

places.name: Rishikesh
places.what: Divine Life Society; sannyasa from Sivananda, 25 February 1949

places.name: Mayapur (Sri Chaitanya Math)
places.what: Settled here after 1904-05; founded Sri Chaitanya Math in 1918

places.name: Agartala, Tripura

places.name: Krishnanagar

glossary.def: Pali for loving-kindness, a Buddhist meditation of wishing wellbeing first to oneself, then to others.
Existence, consciousness and bliss, the traditional description of Brahman. Atmananda rendered the last term as peace.
In Ayyavazhi, one of the chief disciples of Vaikundar, named after the Pandava brothers.
The daily service or worship performed at Ayyavazhi shrines.
Name for groups in Bengal who read the love of Radha and Krishna in a bodily, erotic way; criticised by Bhaktivinoda and Bhaktisiddhanta.
Training in which a person watches a measurement of a body process, such as skin temperature or brain waves, to learn to influence it.
Alternate nostril breathing, taught to balance the breath and calm the nervous system.

issues: dipa-ma: daughter's birth year (Wikipedia 1950) and the details of her death (bowing before a Buddha statue) rest on Wikipedia and Encyclopedia.com; both flagged by Wikipedia as needing citations.
atmananda-krishna-menon: accounts of his realization in 1923 come from student-run sites; the horse-carriage anecdote is as summarised from Renard part one.
ayya-vaikundar: Wikipedia articles disagree on the names of the Seedars and on the penance chronology; the Akilam print date is 1927 or 1933.
chinmayananda: mission site dates the Rishikesh visit to September 1947, a Wikipedia mirror to summer 1947; quotes of the Tapovan tribute come from the mission archive.
bhaktisiddhanta: ages at memorising the Gita (seven or nine) and age at death (62 or 63) differ across sources; Gaura Kishora's initiation date 1900 or 1901.
bhaktivinoda: Wikipedia and devotional chronologies differ on marriage year, cholera year and Hindu College enrolment.

swami-rama: Darbhanga degree dated 1945 (Encyclopedia.com) or 1960 (Hospital Trust); the sealed cave, London, Moscow, Japan claims rest on the Trust alone; the Tigunait biography is titled At the Eleventh Hour (2001) in the chapter, while Encyclopedia.com lists Swami Rama of the Himalayas (1999).
factcheck x_expansion2: see factcheck.unresolved; Ayya Vaikundar pick replaced with G. Patrick (author may prefer another).

dipa-ma: daughter's birth now 'after some twenty-seven years of marriage' (Encyclopedia.com), Wikipedia's 1950 kept as attribution.
dipa-ma: Kreider quotation attributed to Testimonies of Awakening and dipama.com (ledger and page).
dipa-ma: removed 'Always know what you are doing' (absent from dipama.com Essential Quotes and Testimonies).

dipa-ma: death given as September 1989 (Encyclopedia.com), 1 September attributed to Wikipedia; death account restated as the neighbour's report in Encyclopedia.com wording; Wikipedia's version is tagged citation needed.

atmananda: 1919 meeting length given as one night (Stillness Speaks) or day-long (Wikipedia).

ayya-vaikundar: Akilam print date corrected: Ayyavazhi article gives Akilam 1933 and Arul Nool 1927 (footnote 1939/1918); Vaikundar article gives 1939. 1927 was the Arul Nool date.
ayya-vaikundar: Thuvayal Thavasu 'March 1840' reduced to 1840 (month unsupported).
ayya-vaikundar: Seedars named per Historical Vaikundar article (Dharma, Bheeman, Arjunan, Nakulan, Sahadevan); noted Ayyavazhi article also calls Hari Gopalan a Seedar.
ayya-vaikundar: 'especially the giving of food' cut (Teachings article says charity and almsgiving); 'fear no power except himself' changed to 'except Vaikundar' (source wording).

ayya-vaikundar: pick changed from R. Ponnu (unread, not found in a catalogue) to G. Patrick, Religion and Subaltern Agency (University of Madras, 2003), full title from RelBib catalogue; reference 4 updated with the record link.
chinmayananda: Rishikesh visit date given as September 1947 (mission) or summer 1947 (Wikipedia).
chinmayananda: 'about two years' and 'cowshed during 1949 and 1950' replaced with mission wording (more than two years, cowshed, stone for a pillow); the mission page gives no years.
chinmayananda: morning classes 6 to 7 a.m. on Shankara's commentary (mission archive).
bhaktisiddhanta: '(some sources say 7 March)' cut; Wikipedia and the devotional chronology give 27 March or only 1918.
bhaktisiddhanta: 1933 untouchability sentence cut; Wikipedia records only a 1933 reply to Gandhi, not the stated position, and the item is a disputed social remark under SCOPE_PASS_BRIEF.
